decisions.quote:
Overall, our conclusion is that organic food exposure has

much less impact on moral reasoning than found by Eskine,
potentially down to no effect at all. It is not clear why the orig-

inal research reached such a di fferent outcome.
decisions.reason: The record is a completed empirical replication (Studies 1a, 1b, and 2) collecting new data to re-test the published findings of Eskine (2013, first published online in 2012; DOI: 10.1177/1948550612447114, paired with blind target_index 0) that exposure to organic food harshens moral judgments and reduces prosocial behavior. Across two direct replications (Studies 1a and 1b) and an online conceptual replication (Study 2), the authors found negligible effects on both moral judgments (integrated d = 0.06, 95% CI [-0.14, 0.26]) and prosocial behavior (integrated d = 0.03, 95% CI [-0.17, 0.23]) and state an overall verdict that their replication attempts failed to support Eskine's findings.
